newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures slipped slightly on Thursday, largely driven by weaker bond markets in Germany and the U.S., but managed to hold on to most of the heady gains made in the past two sessions.
Traders said many had expected the contract to fill the gap above 127.04 left open yesterday and others took out short positions betting on a move below 127.00.
Stronger than expected German unemployment numbers and a relatively good French government bond auction, however, prompted short covering in the afternoon, traders said.
The December bond future settled down 0.10 at 127.28 after falling as low as 127.08, still leaving a gap above 127.04.
Analysts said the larger-than-expected rise in German unemployment made fears of a German interest rate rise look overdone and could well boost the short end of the curve.
"There's no-way (the Germans) are going to put up rates with unemployment going up like this," Phyllis Reed, bond strategist at BZW Ltd said. "We could see some steepening again."
Damien Jamet, analyst at Fimat said the latest figures coming out of Germany showed there was no need to worry about the Bundesbank's monetary policy.
Analysts said the OAT auction went quite well with demand for the variable rate TEC 10 OAT persisting despite the relative expense of the bond compared to its theoretical value.
One domestic investor was said to have bought 2.3 billion francs of the variable rate OAT.
The overall cover for the sale, which included the TEC, the 6.50 percent 2006 OAT and the current cheapest to deliver OAT, the 8.25 percent 2004 OAT, was 2.7.
The cover was down from 3.1 last month and 3.4 in September but better than some had feared given that yields are at their lowest levels since February 1994.
The European Investment Bank also took advantage of the solid demand for variable rate instruments based on the TEC 10 index to issue 1.5 billion francs of 2006 TEC 10 bonds.

Analysts said domestic investors have been buying the TEC 10 instrument because it offers a higher yield than other money market instruments and allows them to avoid the duration risk of a 10-year bond.
An analyst at a French bank said the bond would also benefit from any curve steepening. "The prospects of seeing the bull market flattening continue are less than seeing some bear market steepening."

As expected the Bank of France and the German Bundesbank both left key money market interest rates unchanged on Thursday. December PIBOR managed to post a small gain as the franc scrambled above 3.38 per mark.
Call money remained unchanged at 3-1/4 3/8 percent.
